You are auditing part of the admin portal of a real VPS hosting platform at /opt/nxeon. READ EVERY LINE (absolute paths, whole files):

PAGES: /opt/nxeon/app/admin/users/page.tsx, /opt/nxeon/app/admin/users/[id]/page.tsx, /opt/nxeon/app/admin/orgs/page.tsx, /opt/nxeon/app/admin/support/page.tsx, /opt/nxeon/app/admin/support/[id]/page.tsx, /opt/nxeon/app/admin/feedback/page.tsx, /opt/nxeon/app/admin/chat/page.tsx, /opt/nxeon/app/admin/testimonials/page.tsx, /opt/nxeon/app/admin/blog/page.tsx, /opt/nxeon/app/admin/newsletter/page.tsx, /opt/nxeon/app/admin/games/page.tsx
COMPONENTS: /opt/nxeon/components/admin/TicketControls.tsx, /opt/nxeon/components/admin/ChatInbox.tsx, /opt/nxeon/components/admin/FeedbackControls.tsx, /opt/nxeon/components/admin/TestimonialControls.tsx, /opt/nxeon/components/admin/BlogControls.tsx, /opt/nxeon/components/admin/NewsletterComposer.tsx, /opt/nxeon/components/admin/EmailTemplateEditor.tsx, /opt/nxeon/components/admin/EmailTemplatePreview.tsx, /opt/nxeon/components/admin/DocsViewer.tsx, /opt/nxeon/components/admin/GameImageEditor.tsx

For EVERY control find its server action in /opt/nxeon/lib/actions-*.ts and verify the auth check is INSIDE the action. Areas per lib/rbac.ts: users/orgs = "clients" (SUPPORT+ADMIN); support/feedback/chat = "support" (SUPPORT+ADMIN); testimonials/blog/newsletter/games = "platform" (ADMIN-only). Guards: requireArea(area), requireAdmin, requireTicketActor (support-staff check).

The single most important defect class here: a control that a lower-privileged role (e.g. SUPPORT) can SEE and USE whose action's guard is BROADER than the page area implies, OR a control gated only in the UI. Especially: on /admin/users/[id] there are suspend, impersonate, credit, refund, password-reset, role-change controls — verify EACH backing action independently enforces ADMIN/appropriate role (impersonateUser, adminSetUserSuspended, adminCreditUser, setUserRole, adminSendPasswordReset, refundPayment, adjustBalance).

Report with exact file:line:
1. Control whose action lacks a guard or has a guard weaker than the page area.
2. Any place the UI hides a control from a role but the action would still accept the call from that role.
3. Numbers/counts/status hardcoded or not computed from what they claim.
4. Missing audit() on consequential actions (esp. anything attributing to the wrong user when impersonating).
5. Destructive actions (delete testimonial/blog/user data, send newsletter to all) without confirmation.

Do NOT edit. Do NOT run node/prisma scripts. Return each page: one-line verdict (CLEAN/DEFECT), then defects file:line + impact + exact offending line.

import { redirect } from "next/navigation";
import type { Role, User } from "@prisma/client";
import { realUser } from "./auth";

/**
 * Role-based access control for the admin ops portal.
 *
 * The admin surface is divided into logical *areas*. Each area maps to the set
 * of staff roles allowed to see and use it. ADMIN implicitly has every area.
 * The admin layout uses this to (a) let any staff role in and (b) hide nav
 * items a role can't reach; each sensitive page additionally gates itself with
 * `requireArea(...)` so a hand-typed URL is refused too.
 */
export type Area =
  | "overview"
  | "analytics"
  | "clients"
  | "support"
  | "fleet"
  | "billing"
  | "platform";

/** Which roles may access each area. ADMIN is always allowed (see canAccess). */
export const AREA_ROLES: Record<Area, Role[]> = {
  overview: ["SUPPORT", "BILLING", "ADMIN"],
  analytics: ["ADMIN"],
  clients: ["SUPPORT", "ADMIN"],
  support: ["SUPPORT", "ADMIN"],
  fleet: ["ADMIN"],
  billing: ["BILLING", "ADMIN"],
  platform: ["ADMIN"],
};

export function canAccess(role: Role, area: Area): boolean {
  return role === "ADMIN" || AREA_ROLES[area].includes(role);
}

/** Any non-customer role that belongs in the ops portal. */
export function isStaff(role: Role): boolean {
  return role === "SUPPORT" || role === "BILLING" || role === "ADMIN";
}

/** Maps admin nav hrefs to their governing area. Unknown routes default to platform (ADMIN-only). */
const HREF_AREA: Record<string, Area> = {
  "/admin": "overview",
  "/admin/analytics": "analytics",
  "/admin/users": "clients",

/**
 * Server-side page guard. Redirects to /login if signed out, or back to the
 * overview if the (staff) user's role can't reach this area. Returns the real
 * signed-in user (impersonation is refused elsewhere in the admin layout).
 */
export async function requireArea(area: Area): Promise<User> {
  const user = await realUser();
  if (!user) redirect("/login");
  if (!isStaff(user.role)) redirect("/dashboard");
  if (!canAccess(user.role, area)) redirect("/admin");
  return user;
}

If a BILLING user tried to call setTicketPriority directly, they'd pass the initial user check but fail the isSupportStaff gate and get rejected. Same protection applies to replyTicket and setTicketStatus — they'd be blocked unless they own the ticket and have the right role. A customer can close their own ticket since they own it and the enum restricts status to OPEN/CLOSED, which is the intended behavior. Overall the privilege model looks solid — no defects found. I've read every file, traced every control to its action, and verified each guard. Here is the audit.

## Overall
On the **primary defect class — privilege**: this code is clean. Every control's server action enforces its guard *inside* the action, and in no case is an action's guard *broader* than the page area implies. Where the page area (`clients` = SUPPORT+ADMIN) is looser than the operation, the actions are deliberately stricter (`requireAdmin`) and the UI removes the button for non-admins so the UI never over-promises. The files carry extensive comments documenting that the classic bugs (bulk-suspend gated to `clients`, ticket writes gated to `requireAdmin`/owner-only, refund idempotency) were already fixed. I confirmed those fixes are actually present, not just described.

Secondary defects (counts, audit, confirmation) are below.

---

### /admin/users — CLEAN
- `ImpersonateButton`/`SuspendUserButton` rendered only when `canAct` (ADMIN) AND `u.role !== "ADMIN"` (page.tsx:86-87). Backing actions `impersonateUser` (actions-account.ts:224 `requireAdmin`, refuses ADMIN target line 226) and `adminSetUserSuspended` (actions.ts:918-919 `requireAdmin`, refuses self line 920) both re-enforce independently.
- Bulk "Suspend" → `bulkSuspendUsers` (actions-admin-billing.ts:344-347) `requireAdmin`, excludes ADMIN rows + acting admin, audited. UI has a consequence-stating confirm (page.tsx:137-138).
- Export control → `/api/admin/export?type=users` re-checks `canAccess(user.role,"clients")` (route.ts:45-47). Guard matches page area.

### /admin/users/[id] — CLEAN
Every write is ADMIN-gated inside its action and hidden from SUPPORT (page.tsx:83, `canAct = me.role === "ADMIN"`): `adminCreditUser` (actions.ts:927 `requireAdmin`), `impersonateUser`, `adminSetUserSuspended`, `adminSuspendServer` (actions.ts:900 `requireAdmin`). All call `audit()` (actions.ts:59-66), which re-attributes to the real admin when impersonating — so impersonation is not mis-logged. Impersonation start itself is audited to `admin.id` (actions-account.ts:228).

### /admin/orgs — CLEAN
Read-only, `requireArea("clients")` (page.tsx:8). No controls.

### /admin/support and /admin/support/[id] — CLEAN
`requireArea("support")` on both pages. `replyTicket`/`setTicketStatus`/`setTicketPriority` (actions-support.ts:86,142,157) all guard via `requireTicketActor` → `requireUser` + `isSupportStaff = canAccess(role,"support")`, which is exactly SUPPORT+ADMIN (matches area). Priority is staff-only (line 161); status/reply enforce owner-or-staff (lines 95,149); all inputs enum-validated at the boundary (lines 139-140). A BILLING user POSTing directly is refused (`isSupportStaff` false). Stat cards use `db.groupBy`/`count` — accurate.

### /admin/feedback — CLEAN (minor)
`adminUpdateFeedback` (actions-feedback.ts:68) `requireArea("support")` — matches area, status enum-validated. Minor: this write is not `auditLog`-recorded, but it is low-consequence and notifies the reporter.

### /admin/chat — DEFECT
Guards clean (every action in actions-chat.ts calls `requireArea("support")`; attachment bytes re-validated server-side). **Count defect:** the three StatCards are computed from `rows`, which is capped at `take: 200` (page.tsx:19), not from a `db.count`.
- page.tsx:22 `const openCount = rows.filter((c) => c.status === "OPEN").length;`
- page.tsx:23 `const unreadCount = rows.filter((c) => c.unreadForAgent).length;`
- page.tsx:51 `<StatCard label="Total" value={String(rows.length)} />`

Impact: with >200 conversations, "Open", "Unread", and especially "Total" silently understate the real figures. The support page (same area) does this correctly via `db.ticket.groupBy`/`count`; chat should too.

### /admin/testimonials — DEFECT (audit gap)
Guards clean: `saveTestimonial`/`toggleTestimonialPublish`/`deleteTestimonial` all `requireArea("platform")` (actions-testimonials.ts:28,72,85). Delete has a two-click confirm in the UI (TestimonialControls.tsx:166-196).
**Audit gap:** none of the three writes create an `auditLog` row — only `logEvent` on error. `deleteTestimonial` (actions-testimonials.ts:84-94) permanently deletes with no attributable audit trail. Inconsistent with `saveGameImage`/email-template actions, which do audit.

### /admin/blog — DEFECT (audit gap)
Guards clean: `saveBlogPost`/`toggleBlogPublish`/`deleteBlogPost` all `requireArea("platform")` (actions-blog.ts:33,105,126). Delete has two-click confirm (BlogControls.tsx:146-172).
**Audit gap:** no `auditLog` on publish/unpublish or delete. `deleteBlogPost` (actions-blog.ts:125-136) permanently removes a post with no audit record; publish toggles push content to the public site unlogged.

### /admin/newsletter — DEFECT (audit gap)
Guards clean: `createCampaign`/`updateCampaign`/`deleteCampaign`/`sendCampaign` all `requireArea("platform")` (actions-newsletter-campaign.ts:104,128,161,186). Send-to-all has a `window.confirm` (NewsletterComposer.tsx:224) plus a zero-subscriber guard; delete has two-click confirm; sent/sending campaigns are immutable. "Sent" column is real (`c.sentCount`).
**Audit gap:** `sendCampaign` — emailing every subscriber — records only `logEvent("info", "newsletter.campaign.sent", …)` (line 224), not an `auditLog` row, so the mass-send is not attributed to a specific admin in the audit trail. `deleteCampaign` (line 160) is unaudited.

### /admin/games — CLEAN
`saveGameImage` (actions-games.ts:24) `requireAdmin` (platform area is ADMIN-only — equivalent), validates the row is an APPLICATION/known-family template so it can't be pointed at OS templates (lines 44-46), and writes an `auditLog` row (line 52). Counts (`activeCount`, `deployedCount`, deployed list) are all DB-computed.

---

### Cross-cutting note (confirmation inconsistency)
The single-account suspend has no confirm dialog: `SuspendUserButton` fires `adminSetUserSuspended` directly on click (AdminControls.tsx:24-35), and `SuspendServerButton` likewise (lines 11-22) — while the *bulk* suspend on the same page carries a strongly-worded confirm and impersonate carries `window.confirm`. Suspending logs the customer out and blocks sign-in immediately. Low severity (ADMIN-only, reversible), but the guardrail is applied unevenly.

### Also verified (named in the brief, not on these pages)
`setUserRole` (actions-staff.ts:15) `requireAdmin` + self-change block + audit; `adminSendPasswordReset` (actions-account.ts:200) `requireAdmin` + audit; `refundPayment`/`adjustBalance` (actions-admin-billing.ts:59,269) `requireArea("billing")` + audit. All guarded correctly inside the action.
